name: Institute on Neuroscience (ION) Summer Research Program
org: Georgia State University, Center for Behavioral Neuroscience
what_you_do: Do paid summer research in a Georgia State neuroscience lab with a faculty mentor. You start with a fruit fly lab course, go to weekly workshops, then present your results at a symposium.
who_can_apply: High school students who excel in science and are interested in research. The minimum age is 16. Competitive.
pay_detail: Stipend. The 2025 rate was $4,500; the page says the 2026 rate was not guaranteed. MARTA passes or parking may be reimbursed.
duration: About 6 weeks, 40 hours a week. In 2026 it ran June 22 to a symposium on August 6.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed June 14, 2026, a late, short cycle because funding was delayed. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Online application form, then an interview. You may not miss any starred program dates and may miss at most one week of lab time.
notes: Funding for 2026 came from the Army Educational Outreach Program, so the dates and stipend can change from year to year. Bring your own meals and get yourself to downtown Atlanta daily. No housing is provided. Join the ION email list on the home page to hear about 2027.
